questions.q: According to the summary, roughly how much of the day do we spend indoors?
a: Almost 90%
Almost 50%
Almost 70%
Almost 99%
questions.why: The overview says we spend close to 90% of each day inside, which the book links to poorer health.

questions.q: What is forest bathing as the summary describes it?
a: A Japanese practice of immersing yourself in nature
A guided workout routine performed among trees
A method for growing plants inside the home
A silent meditation that avoids all movement
questions.why: The overview introduces shinrin-yoku, a Japanese form of forest therapy built on immersion in nature.

questions.q: Once you have found a good spot to forest-bathe, what should you do?
a: Do nothing, admire the patterns and focus on breathing
Walk briskly until you break a sweat
Recite a mantra out loud for ten minutes
Take photos to record everything you see
questions.why: The first lesson says the task is simply to stop, take in nature's patterns and concentrate on your breath.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you ground yourself in nature?
a: Walk barefoot on grass or soil for about 20 minutes
Sit against a tree for an hour every morning
Breathe deeply while standing in shallow water
Lie on rocks until your skin feels cool
questions.why: The second lesson says nature's low electric charge balances our electrons, and barefoot walking helps.

questions.q: What do essential oils such as pine and redwood release?
a: Phytoncides, which are antimicrobial compounds
Negative ions that clean the surrounding air
Carbon dioxide that feeds nearby plants
Antioxidants that protect against sunlight
questions.why: The third lesson says oils like these recreate a forest atmosphere and give off phytoncides.
